correctness.rationale: For a vertex of degree d and s agreeing ordinary neighbors, the closed-neighborhood minority flip condition is 2s>d−1 and the energy decrement is 2(2s−d). All rim degrees equal three, so only the even-degree hub can flip neutrally. A nonabsorbing energy plateau contains at most the two hub orientations and its first-step equations give expected exit time at most 3(n+1). Every strict drop is at least two from E(c)≤4n; the strong Markov property proves E_c[T]≤(3/2)(n+1)E(c)≤6n(n+1). Rim inactivity is equivalent to excluding 00 and 111 cyclically; its gap-count formula and the 3-state transfer matrix establish 2P_n recurrent configurations with precisely the specified parity decomposition. Exhaustive finite SCC checks for n=3..11 passed, but are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete Markov recurrent-class classification on the nonbipartite wheel family, exact density-resolved counts, a parity-driven existence/nonexistence of moving attractors, and an explicit uniform quadratic expected time to reach those classes. Unlike the previously known Perrin count alone, the stochastic convergence bound and class decomposition provide structural information about dynamics and contrasting behavior across graph topologies.
